Formulation
Current presentation involves an acute flare of chronic atopic dermatitis with significant pruritus and skin cracking. Predisposing factors include personal history of eczema and asthma plus family atopy. Precipitating factors not explored. Perpetuating factors may include inadequate potency of topical steroid. Protective factors include willingness to engage in treatment and existing emollient routine.

Mental Health Care Plan Details

Principal Problem: Worsening eczema
- Patient Goal(s):
  • Reduce itch, redness, and soreness over the next two weeks  
- Clinical Goal(s):
  • Decrease inflammatory skin lesions and pruritus; prevent secondary infection
- Actions (Patient):
  • Apply Betnovate cream thinly twice daily for two weeks  
  • Continue Diprobase and Dermol as regular emollients  
  • Take prescribed Fexofenadine as directed  
  • Monitor for adverse reactions; seek review if no improvement or worsening
- Actions (Clinician/GP):
  • Send electronic prescriptions for Fexofenadine and Betnovate to Boots pharmacy  
  • Provide guidance on fingertip-unit dosing  
  • Arrange follow-up if patient contacts earlier or at two-week mark

Secondary Problem: Asthma (stable)
- Patient Goal(s): Not recorded
- Clinical Goal(s): Maintain control; PRN salbutamol use only
- Actions (Patient): Use blue inhaler as needed
- Actions (Clinician/GP): Not recorded

Patient Education, Emergency Care & Relapse Prevention
- Education Given: Yes. Topics Covered: Use of potent topical steroid, fingertip-unit quantity, continuation of emollients, when to seek further care
- Early Warning Signs of Relapse/Worsening: Increasing itch, spread of rash, weeping/exudate, lack of response after two weeks
- Coping Strategies: Adherence to emollient regimen; avoid scratching; return for review if needed
